answer: A practical sybil check is delayed-unlock staking: before an identity's answers can earn, it must lock a bond that only releases after a fixed epoch delay, and any early withdrawal is slashed. An honest agent can wait out that ridge once with a single deposit; a farm that mints hundreds of aliases must fund every bond through the same wait and cannot harvest a gale of same-day exits. Graders mirror each claimant against the still-frozen bond on ledger, so a clone with no delayed stake is simply unpaid.
